title: [Bug] 'highlight' is not recognized as a valid pseudo-element, even though it is present in `src/selector`
fixedBy: df63db2 Add support for `::highlight` (#970), first released in v1.33.0 (2026-07-19)
impact: 4 reactions. Historically medium: every ::highlight() rule warned in 1.32.0 and earlier (output was still passed through unchanged, so only a spurious warning, or a build failure for tools that promote warnings). Same root cause as closed #861/#1017.
summary: In 1.32.0 and earlier, ::highlight(name) was parsed as an unknown pseudo-element and produced the 'not recognized' warning. PR #970 (commit df63db2) added HighlightFunction; it shipped in 1.33.0, 12 days before this issue was filed. 1.33.0 and master parse it with no warning, in strict and errorRecovery mode and with the reporter's chrome 95 targets. The reporter most likely ran an older lightningcss (bundled by a tool, or a stale playground build).
repro: 1300-repro.mjs. `::highlight(my-custom-highlight){background-color:peachpuff}` with targets chrome 95 -> local/1.33.0: `::highlight(my-custom-highlight){background-color:#ffdab9}` with no warnings; 1.32.0/1.31.1: same output plus the warning "'highlight' is not recognized as a valid pseudo-element".
evidence: scripts/repro.mjs on local (master c6a0c3c), 1.33.0, 1.32.0, 1.31.1: all 4 cases flip WRONG->correct at 1.33.0. `git tag --contains df63db2` = v1.33.0. A control shows that the compat check (Feature::Highlight, chrome 105) correctly blocks merging two ::highlight rules into one selector list for chrome 95 targets, and allows it for chrome 110.
draftReply:
Thanks for the report! `::highlight()` support landed in #970 and was first released in **v1.33.0** (July 19). With 1.33.0 your example compiles with no warning:

```css
::highlight(my-custom-highlight){background-color:#ffdab9}
```

In 1.32.0 and earlier it warns as you describe. The rule was still passed through unchanged, so only the warning was wrong. If you still see it, please check which `lightningcss` version is actually installed (tools like Vite or Tailwind can pull in an older one: `npm ls lightningcss`). If it still warns on 1.33.0, could you share the exact version and options? Closing as fixed for now.
